The word-splitting addition is correct and needed (that part fixes `test_long_words_are_split`, `test_width_of_one`, etc.). However, the diff also silently changes the line-fill comparison from `<=` to `<`:

```
-        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
+        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width:
```

This contradicts the docstring, which explicitly says a word is appended "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long" (i.e. `<=`). The original `<=` comparison was already correct and was not the cause of the failing tests — I verified that keeping `<=` alongside the new word-splitting logic makes every test in `tests/test_wrap.py` pass. The switch to strict `<` is unnecessary and introduces an off-by-one bug: any input where a word fits exactly at the width boundary (e.g. `wrap_text("ab cd", 5)`) will now be split into two lines (`["ab", "cd"]`) instead of the one line (`["ab cd"]`) the docstring requires. None of the existing tests happen to exercise that exact-boundary case, so it slips through, but it's a real behavioral regression relative to the documented contract.

Please revert that one comparison back to `<=` and keep the rest of the word-splitting fix.
